https://business-review.eu/money/stock-e.text: Divo Pulitika, InterCapital ETF: Romania-focused ETFs add 276 million euros in assets in seven months, almost tripling in size Romania-focused ETFs listed on the Bucharest Stock Exchange added 276 million euros in assets in the first seven months of 2026, almost tripling in size from 174 million euros at the end of 2025 to approximately 450 million euros at the end of July. Of this increase, an estimated 155 million euros came from fresh investor inflows, while approximately 122 million euros was generated by the appreciation of Romanian equities. The six locally listed Romania-focused ETFs now hold assets equivalent to approximately 1.3% of the entire free float of the Bucharest Stock Exchange. Analysis by Divo Pulitika, Board Member, InterCapital ETF At the same time, Romania is increasingly present in the portfolios of international ETFs. At the end of June, 28 foreign-listed ETFs with almost 500 billion euros in combined assets had exposure to Romanian equities, holding approximately 264 million euros in Romanian companies. While Romania represents only around 0.05% of the total assets of these funds, their Romanian holdings are already approaching 1% of the entire free float of the Bucharest Stock Exchange. The funds are managed by 12 international providers, including some of the world’s largest asset managers, such as Vanguard, Invesco, JPMorgan and Xtrackers. These developments are part of a much larger structural shift taking place across financial markets. ETFs continue to be one of the fastest-growing and most dynamic segments of the financial industry. Technology has made buying and selling ETFs increasingly simple and cost-efficient, while the range of products available to investors has expanded far beyond the world’s largest equity indices into individual countries, regions, sectors and increasingly specialized investment themes. Read more about BVB reaches 10 listed ETFs with launch of Globinvest BET-XT fund read more According to Bloomberg data, ETFs listed on European exchanges currently hold approximately 3.3 trillion euros in assets, around three quarters of which are invested in equities. To put this into perspective, this is approximately 40 times the combined market capitalization of all Romanian listed companies. Europe is also heading towards another record year for ETF investment. Since the beginning of 2026, investors have directed approximately 280 billion euros of new money into European-listed ETFs, already equivalent to around 86% of the record inflows registered during the whole of 2025. European investors continue to favour diversified portfolios. Slightly more than half of this year’s net inflows went into internationally diversified ETFs, such as products tracking global indices including MSCI World. US-focused ETFs, predominantly those providing exposure to the S&P 500, attracted around 21% of net inflows, while Europe-focused products, including both country-specific and broader continental strategies, accounted for another 15%. The remaining 13% went to ETFs covering markets such as Asia, BRICS and other geographies. The expansion of the global ETF industry is increasingly relevant for Romania because these products have become an important channel through which international capital reaches individual markets. Since the beginning of 2026, the value of Romanian equities held by foreign ETFs has increased by approximately 31 million euros. Interestingly, however, this increase was driven by the appreciation of Romanian shares rather than by fresh investment. On a net basis, foreign ETFs recorded an estimated 34 million euros of outflows from Romanian equities during the period. A large part of these outflows can be explained by index mechanics rather than by a broader withdrawal of international ETF capital from Romania. Many of the foreign ETFs with Romanian exposure track FTSE indices, which excluded OMV Petrom during their March rebalancing. This triggered estimated ETF sales of approximately 52 million euros of OMV Petrom shares. At the same time, around 18 million euros was added to other Romanian companies, led by Banca Transilvania with approximately 9 million euros, Hidroelectrica with 4 million euros, Nuclearelectrica with 3 million euros and Electrica with 1 million euros, alongside smaller additions to other issuers. The exclusion of OMV Petrom may appear surprising considering that the company remains one of the major constituents of Romania’s domestic BET index. International index providers, however, assess more than free-float market capitalization and absolute trading volumes. Another important factor is free-float turnover velocity, which measures how frequently the shares available to minority investors actually change hands. A company can therefore have both a substantial free float and significant trading volumes, but still fail an index liquidity test if those volumes are low relative to the size of its freely tradable shares. This highlights a broader challenge for the Romanian capital market. Free-float velocity in Romania has improved this year and currently stands at approximately 24%, meaning that the equivalent of 24% of the market’s free float changes hands annually. This is comparable with Croatia at around 20%, but remains considerably below other regional markets such as Hungary at 78%, Czechia at 101% and Poland at 192%. Part of the explanation can be found in the structure of the domestic investor base. Large Romanian institutional investors, particularly pension funds, tend to be long-term holders, while domestic retail trading remains less active than in some neighbouring markets. At the same time, participation from larger foreign investors remains constrained partly by perceived country uncertainty and partly by Romania’s continued classification as a Frontier market by some major international index providers, such as Morgan Stanley Capital International (MSCI). This can create a circular challenge for the development of the market: lower international participation contributes to lower liquidity, while lower liquidity can itself limit index inclusion and weighting, consequently restricting the passive investment flows that greater representation in international indices could generate. At the same time, one of the most important developments of 2026 is that the strongest ETF-driven inflows into Romanian equities are increasingly coming from the domestic market itself. The estimated 155 million euros of net inflows into Romania-focused ETFs listed on BVB represents fresh investor capital, with the majority of these inflows coming from Romanian retail investors. This is particularly notable considering how recently the local ETF market began to develop: InterCapital ETF launched the first ETF tracking the BET-TRN index on the Bucharest Stock Exchange on May 29, 2024. Since then, the market has expanded rapidly, with six Romania-focused ETFs now listed on BVB and their combined assets reaching approximately 450 million euros. The timing has also been supportive. The Romanian equity market delivered the highest 10-year total return among the global markets analysed by InterCapital ETF, while 2026 has brought another approximately 50% increase so far. At the same time, the entry of major Romanian banking groups into the ETF segment has substantially increased the visibility, accessibility and distribution of these products among local investors, helping transform ETFs from a niche investment instrument into an increasingly relevant part of the Romanian capital market. ETFs are also becoming increasingly relevant for the Bucharest Stock Exchange beyond the capital they channel into the underlying Romanian companies. ETF units themselves are actively traded securities. Since the beginning of 2026, approximately 165 million euros worth of ETF units have been traded on BVB, representing around 6.2% of total equity turnover. For a segment that was almost negligible on the Romanian market only a few years ago, this represents a significant change. The figure is also notable when compared internationally, being broadly in line with the Netherlands, one of Europe’s established ETF hubs, and ahead of markets such as Spain at 0.3%, Hungary at 0.9%, Poland at 1.1%, Japan at 4.8% and France at 5.7%. ETF penetration remains higher in markets such as Croatia at around 10%, Italy at 13%, the UK at 20%, Germany at 22% and the US at approximately 30%, suggesting that there remains considerable room for further development in Romania. What was until recently an almost negligible segment of the Bucharest Stock Exchange is therefore becoming increasingly relevant on several levels. International ETFs connect Romanian companies with some of the world’s largest pools of investment assets, locally listed ETFs are bringing significant new retail capital into Romanian equities, and trading in ETF units themselves is becoming a meaningful contributor to BVB turnover. As the segment develops, these effects can reinforce each other: broader distribution can attract more investors, higher ETF assets can translate into additional investment in the underlying companies, and greater trading activity can contribute to the liquidity and visibility of the Romanian capital market. ETFs are likely to continue playing a growing role in this process. At the same time, their development gives Romanian investors an increasingly simple way to diversify beyond their domestic market, including into other Central and Eastern European economies that have historically received less attention from international investors. Diversification remains important over longer investment horizons, and the growing availability of international and regional ETFs directly on the Bucharest Stock Exchange means that investing abroad increasingly does not require leaving the local market infrastructure. As BVB develops and local demand grows, the range of markets accessible to Romanian investors through locally traded ETFs is likely to expand further. Note: Foreign ETF data as of end-June 2026, the latest comparable period available for all funds included in the analysis. Romanian-listed ETF assets and trading data as of end-July 2026. Sources: Bloomberg, InterCapital ETF. About Đivo Pulitika Đivo Pulitika is a Board Member at InterCapital ETF. Pulitika began his career in the financial industry while studying at the Faculty of Economics and Business in Zagreb, initially joining Intercapital’s analysis department. Over time, he became the head of this department, where he focused on promoting investments in regional capital markets, conducting stock valuations, and organizing roadshows and conferences for clients. In 2019, he transitioned to InterCapital Asset Management, Croatia’s leading asset management company at a time, where he led the equity analysis department and later became portfolio manager. Pulitika was also responsible for preparing and implementing policies on responsible and sustainable investing. He participated in the creation of InterCapital’s first ETFs from their beginning, and officially took over as their fund manager at the beginning of 2023. His expertise and leadership have significantly contributed to the firm’s success in managing investment funds and individual portfolios for a wide range of clients. With the creation of InterCapital ETF as a separate company in May 2025, Pulitika was appointed Member of the Management Board in charge of further growing the ETF business. https://www.politico.eu/article/canada-m.text: Trump is nowhere and yet everywhere in Carney's speech U.S. President Donald Trump has not been mentioned once in Mark Carney's address so far, and yet he clearly loomed large over Strasbourg. "I want to be precise about what I am not proposing. I am not proposing a third bloc in order to become a great-power rival — only with better manners," Carney said, in a thinly veiled dig at Trump. "We do not seek power to dominate others. On the contrary, we are pursuing resilience so that no one can control our open markets, impair our sovereignty, threaten our territorial integrity, or undermine our freedoms, our democracies, our rule of law," he said, to the claps of lawmakers in the room. "It's these motivations, combined with our latent hard power, mean we can help to create the next just, stable, and prosperous world order," he added, echoing his pitch at the World Economic Forum in Davos earlier this year, where he called for the world’s “middle powers” to stand together against autocrats.

The discussions reportedly focus on the potential electoral gains of political forces seeking to change their countries’ current approach to supporting Ukraine, including France’s National Rally and Germany’s Alternative for Germany (AfD). However, European officials told Reuters that the European Union would remain capable of supporting Kyiv despite potential shifts in the positions of individual member states. Lithuanian Foreign Minister Kestutis Budrys said the forthcoming elections were among the factors being considered when assessing the prospects for future assistance to Ukraine.
